exposure: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery-Cesarean Delivery (ERAS-CD) protocol practices (e.g., perioperative information, antibiotic prophylaxis, intravenous fluids, skin cleansing, analgesics, discharge information, preoperative fasting time, postoperative first oral intake time, initiating breastfeeding time)
cohort: The study included 333 women with a mean gestational age of 38.38 weeks who underwent elective cesarean section, with 58.9% having a repeat CS and 38.7% multiple repeat CS.
finding: While the ERAS-CD protocol was generally applied, preoperative fasting time, postoperative first oral intake time, and initiating breastfeeding time were longer than optimal, and mobilization time, need for analgesics, and drain application significantly affected oral feeding initiation, breastfeeding initiation, and length of hospital stay.
mod_finding: For women undergoing elective cesarean sections, key recovery metrics like preoperative fasting, postoperative first oral intake, and breastfeeding initiation times were prolonged despite general adherence to the ERAS-CD protocol, with mobilization, analgesia, and drain use impacting recovery.
